solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fairground ride is to revert to previous state

definitions.meaning: a roller coaster with steep ups and downs
to ... is to return to how things were before

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry gone odd: a fairground ride defined as going back to how things were.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a zigzag roller coaster; the two-word phrasal verb means return to an earlier condition.

clue.text: Girl taking tin round America

indicators.note: taking means the tin symbol takes another piece into itself
the tin symbol takes the abbreviation for America inside it, wrapping round it

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A girl carrying a tin around the United States, perhaps collecting for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan is a common female first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Virgin excited by capital composer

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so the letters of virgin are shaken into a new order

parts.note: Berlin is the capital of Germany

explanation.surface: A virgin thrilled by a city, or by money, alongside a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin was the American songwriter of White Christmas and many other popular standards.

clue.text: Miraculous place is able to amaze at the start

parts.note: can means is able to

indicators.note: at the start means only the first letter of amaze is taken

explanation.surface: A wonder-working place that can astonish visitors from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospel of John, Jesus turned water into wine at the wedding at Cana, his first miracle.

clue.text: Two very common verbs cause no trouble

parts.note: the first of two very common verbs is to be
the second of the common verbs is to have

explanation.surface: A grammar note about everyday verbs, oddly glossed as keeping out of mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two very common verbs' as a whole gives BE and HAVE, two of the commonest verbs in English, joined together.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave is to act properly, the opposite of making a nuisance of yourself.

clue.text: Trick rather obvious? Sorry!

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
trite means hackneyed, too obvious to be interesting

explanation.surface: Someone apologising for pulling a trick that was far too easy to spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrite means feeling remorse, the state of someone who says they are sorry.

clue.text: Role with lines: not coming out with them all?

definitions.meaning: in theatre a ... is a role in which the actor has lines to say

definitions.text: not coming out with them all?
definitions.meaning: read literally, speaking only part of the lines, not delivering all of them

explanation.surface: An actor with lines who somehow doesn't deliver all of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical role with dialogue, as opposed to a walk-on; jokingly, speaking only a portion.

clue.text: On the shelf, pawn love token

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece on another sits above it, so the pawn letter goes first

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn
a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: An unmarried woman 'on the shelf' pawns a keepsake from a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the shelf' is the British idiom for someone thought too old to marry, a romantic red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is a promise or a token of commitment, such as a gift given in love.

clue.text: Quiet about incident, far from the first

indicators.note: about means the quiet letters go round the other piece

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
an event is an incident or occurrence

explanation.surface: Hushing up an incident that was nowhere near the first of its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventh place in a sequence is well down the order, a long way from first.

clue.text: Fine palace, outside demolished, in republic

indicators.note: with the outer letters of the phrase knocked away, what remains inside is the answer

explanation.surface: A fine palace whose outer walls have been knocked down, somewhere in a republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal, the Himalayan country, became a federal republic in 2008 when its monarchy was abolished.

clue.text: Not a single sister is heard

indicators.note: is heard means the word for sister is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister

explanation.surface: Silence in the convent: not one sister makes a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: None means not any, not even one.

clue.text: In van rode wildly around lake, avoiding the water

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the abbreviation for lake
wildly means the letters of van rode are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone in a van drove recklessly around a lake, keeping out of the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges VANRODE into OVERAND, and 'around' places L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An overland route goes by land rather than by sea or river.

clue.text: Guards hat from worrying break-ins

indicators.note: worrying shakes the letters of break-ins, as a dog worries a bone, into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier's headgear seen as a source of anxiety about burglaries.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearskin is the tall black fur cap worn by the Guards regiments outside Buckingham Palace.

clue.text: Lie about what is in roughage

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
re means about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Someone fibbing about what their high-fibre diet actually contains.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughage is dietary fibre, the indigestible plant material found in such food.

clue.text: Al with this painting would be in the open air

definitions.text: Al with this painting would be in the open air

parts.words: Al with this painting would be in the open air
parts.note: a name like Al placed before this painting word gives the phrase meaning outdoors

explanation.walkthrough: Put AL in front of the answer and you get 'al fresco', meaning outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a mural painted onto fresh wet plaster.

clue.text: Wind's double force in the end

parts.note: a twin is a double, an exact counterpart

indicators.note: in the end means only the final letter of force is used

explanation.surface: A wind that doubles its force, finally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind's' is 'Wind is', so the definition is the verb wind, as in coiling.
explanation.definitionFit: Twine is to wind or twist something round, as a vine twines round a post.

clue.text: Sound like a cow in school, but get kissing

indicators.note: in means the cow's sound is set inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: to moo is to make a cow's sound

explanation.surface: Pupils lowing like cattle in class, then turning to snogging.
explanation.definitionFit: To smooch is to kiss and cuddle amorously.

clue.text: Parts of hearing as murder is dissected

indicators.note: dissected means the letters are cut up and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A court hearing where a murder case is examined piece by piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dissected' rearranges ASMURDER. 'Hearing' sounds like a trial but means the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The eardrums are membranes in the ears, organs essential to the sense of hearing.

clue.text: A good artist in Indian city

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A fine painter living in a city in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra, in Uttar Pradesh, is the city of the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Set of maps a sailor put up

indicators.note: put up means read upwards, which in a down answer reverses the letters

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor setting up a book of charts.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound collection of maps.

clue.text: Some share a ride back

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Passengers sharing a lift, some in the back seat.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear of something is its back part.

clue.text: Part of chain put on Charlie in prison

indicators.note: the chain piece is put on after the Charlie letter

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a link is one ring of a chain

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie being chained up in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The clink is British slang for jail.

clue.text: This protective garment superior to the rest?

definitions.meaning: a loose coat or one-piece suit worn over clothes to protect them
read as two words, ..., being above everyone else

explanation.surface: Asking whether a work garment outranks all other clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall is protective workwear; split, it means ranking above everyone.

clue.text: Hermits confused in chain store

indicators.note: confused means the letters of chain store are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Recluses bewildered by a busy high-street shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchorites are religious recluses who withdraw from the world, the same as hermits.
